description: Ireland: how much of a redundancy or severance package is tax-free and the tax on the rest (Revenue Tax and Duty Manual Part 05-05-19, March 2026). Statutory redundancy is exempt; of the ex-gratia lump sum, the highest of the basic exemption (€10,160 + €765 per complete year), the increased exemption (+€10,000 less any tax-free pension lump sum, if not claimed in the last 10 years) and SCSB (average pay × years ÷ 15, less the pension lump sum) is tax-free, capped at €200,000 for life; the excess is taxed as pay (income tax and USC, not PRSI). Also shows the result if the pension lump sum is given up. Reproduces Revenue's 11 worked examples. Use this when someone in Ireland asks how much tax they will pay on a redundancy or severance payment.

avgPay.description: Average annual taxable pay over the last 36 months, EUR

claimedIn10Years.description: Received more than the basic exemption on a termination payment in the last 10 years (default false)

lumpSum.description: Severance on top of statutory redundancy (ex-gratia, non-contractual), EUR

months.description: Extra months beyond the complete years (default 0)

payThisYear.description: Other taxable pay in the same tax year, EUR (default 0)

pensionLumpSum.description: Tax-free pension lump sum from this job (received or due later), EUR (default 0)

priorExempt.description: Exemptions already used on earlier payments, EUR (default 0)

redundancy.description: Genuine redundancy with 2+ years service, so statutory redundancy is due (default true)

waive.description: Irrevocably give up that pension lump sum (default false)

weeklyPay.description: Gross weekly pay now, EUR (for statutory redundancy; default avgPay / 52)

year.description: Tax year of the payment, 2026 or 2027 (default 2026)
